regions.name: Jezero Crater (Perseverance)
regions.terrainType: Crater floor with ancient river delta

atmosphere.notes: MEDA measured ~718 Pa shortly after landing. Pressure computed from elevation with NSSDC values (6.36 mb at mean radius, scale height 11.0 km); global pressure varies 4.0-8.7 mb with season.

humidity.notes: Liquid water unstable at the surface

obstacles: Frequent dust devils (most of any Mars landing site)

geology.description: Crater floor of igneous rocks altered by water; Fe-Mg carbonates indicate reaction with CO2-rich water; voids hold sulfates and perchlorates.

sources.title: Rodriguez-Manfredi et al. 2023, The diverse meteorology of Jezero crater (Nature Geoscience)
Perseverance MEDA weather instrument overview
Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit - Quick Facts
Farley et al. 2022, Aqueously altered igneous rocks sampled on the floor of Jezero crater (Science)
Mars Fact Sheet

regions.name: Gale Crater - Aeolis Mons base (Curiosity)
regions.terrainType: Crater floor and layered central mound

notableCompounds: Methane (trace, ~0.4 ppb average; spike to ~7 ppb)

atmosphere.notes: Largest diurnal pressure variations seen by any lander (REMS). Pressure computed from elevation with NSSDC values (6.36 mb at mean radius, scale height 11.0 km); global pressure varies 4.0-8.7 mb with season.

humidity.notes: REMS: very dry, never reached saturation; RH up to 70% on winter nights; vapor 1,000-10,000x less than Earth

geology.description: Ancient lake basin recording a habitable environment; Curiosity climbed ~740 m up Mount Sharp by sol 3967.

sources.title: Gomez-Elvira et al. 2014, Curiosity's REMS: Overview of the first 100 sols (JGR Planets)
